Description - POST /services/ChomikBoxService.svc

How the endpoint reacts to requests that do not match an operation (all verified live):

  • unknown SOAPAction (e.g. …/NonExistingMethod, or …/SessionBegin, which the main service does not implement): a:ActionNotSupported, HTTP 500. Exactly 17 of the client's 18 actions exist;
  • missing SOAPAction: a:ActionNotSupported (Action '');
  • operation element in http://chomikuj.pl (no trailing slash): parameters not matched, a:InternalServiceFault;
  • a value that cannot be deserialised, including an empty element or an out-of-range Int32 (e.g. ModifyFolder freePoints=2147483648): a:DeserializationFailed naming the parameter and CLR type (the oracle used to establish every parameter name, type and order);
  • Content-Type: application/soap+xml (SOAP 1.2): HTTP 415 (the binding is SOAP 1.1, basicHttpBinding-style).

Path notes

The real URL every SOAP operation is posted to. Documented here for service-level behaviour; the per-operation paths (/Auth, /Folders, …) describe the operations themselves.

Main endpoint not supported request main-endpoint-not-supported

Captured live on 2026-10-24T15:27:01Z: POST http://box.chomikuj.pl/services/ChomikBoxService.svc. Request: SOAPAction: http://chomikuj.pl/IChomikBoxService/SessionBegin, Content-Encoding: gzip (171 bytes on the wire, 250 uncompressed; the example shows the uncompressed XML).

SessionBegin (name, passHash, ver, client{name,version,os}) belongs to the separate session server http://session.box.chomikuj.pl/session, used only when session-enabled=true (default false). That host does not resolve in DNS (checked at capture time: false), so it was never called with credentials. Sent here WITHOUT parameters to the main service: a:ActionNotSupported, i.e. it is not part of IChomikBoxService.

500

SOAP fault.

Schema text/xml

Schema SoapFaultEnvelope, as an XML element tree in wire order. Namespaces are shown where they change.

  • <s:Envelope> object required SoapFaultEnvelope xmlns http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/

    SOAP 1.1 fault envelope (HTTP 500, Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8, never gzip-compressed).

    • <s:Body> object required
      • <s:Fault> object required SoapFault

        The fault.

        • <faultcode> string required no namespace

          Qualified fault code with its own namespace declaration on the element: a:InternalServiceFault and a:DeserializationFailed (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/net/2005/12/windowscommunicationfoundation/dispatcher), a:ActionNotSupported and a:DestinationUnreachable (a = http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2005/05/addressing/none).

        • <faultstring> object required no namespace

          Human-readable message. DeserializationFailed names the parameter and CLR type, which is how the contract was established.

          • @xml:lang string required namespace http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace

            Language of the message (en-US).

          • text content string required

            Message text.

Client vs live - discrepancies

Security notes - findings that concern POST /services/ChomikBoxService.svc

  • S-06 Low Out-of-order or wrong-namespace parameters are silently dropped (null/0); some malformed requests (operation element without the trailing slash, the hamsterId/folderId Download id, an empty Auth) trigger an unhandled a:InternalServiceFault. The client's own "download folder" action builds exactly that hamsterId/folderId id, so that feature presumably fails against today's server (Inferred).
  • S-07 Low Contract disclosure through faults and headers: a:DeserializationFailed names parameters and CLR types, a:DestinationUnreachable leaks internal origin host names, and responses carry x-powered-by: ASP.NET and x-server.

From x-security-notes in the spec. Ratings and scope are explained on Security & privacy.
